brief: GS's morning TMT note leads with a coordinated overnight selloff across global tech/AI/semis after China's CXMT claimed a memory-chip breakthrough (a 4F² design launching before year-end) that would place it ahead of Samsung and SK Hynix despite US sanctions on tool access; Musk's comments on China's manufacturing scale added to the pressure. Korea, Japan and Europe tech all fell, Kioxia and ASML dropped, and WDC, STX, MU and SNDK are down premarket, with SOXX on a sixth straight down day and Broadcom's CEO warning of overheating sentiment; ASML and TSM report this week. Separately: Applied Materials expects to double revenue without doubling headcount via AI; Alibaba priced new AI glasses near Meta's Ray-Ban level while Meta added a cheaper camera-free Muse model; China smartphone shipments fell a sixth straight quarter as Huawei grew and Apple's China volumes slipped. On earnings, JPM fell premarket on a FICC miss as bank earnings open Q3 season; GS previewed StubHub (GMS estimate above consensus, revenue estimate below, price target cut to $11) and its Live Entertainment coverage.
